quiz.title: Matrices Miscellaneous Exercise Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight mixed questions on the miscellaneous exercise topics — matrix polynomials, inverses, symmetric and skew-symmetric parts, and matrix equations. Answer each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: A² = A·A. Row 1 × columns gives [[0,0],[0,0]], so A² = O. Such a matrix is called nilpotent.

questions.q: A square matrix A can always be written as the sum of which two matrices?
options: A symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix
A diagonal and an identity matrix
questions.explanation: A = ½(A + A′) + ½(A − A′). The first part is symmetric, the second is skew-symmetric.

questions.q: For the symmetric part ½(A + A′) to exist and be defined, A must be
questions.explanation: A′ can only be added to A when both have the same order, which requires A to be square.

questions.q: If A is invertible and satisfies A² − 4A + 3I = O, then A⁻¹ equals
questions.explanation: From A² − 4A + 3I = O, multiply by A⁻¹: A − 4I + 3A⁻¹ = O, so A⁻¹ = ⅓(4I − A).

questions.explanation: Skew-symmetry means aₕₖ = −aₖₕ. For a diagonal entry aₕₕ = −aₕₕ, which forces aₕₕ = 0.

questions.explanation: A matrix equal to its own transpose (A′ = A) is symmetric.

If X is a 2×2 matrix and AX = B with A invertible, then X equals
questions.explanation: Left-multiply both sides by A⁻¹: A⁻¹AX = A⁻¹B, so X = A⁻¹B. Order matters — you must pre-multiply.

faq.q: What kinds of problems appear in the Class 12 Matrices miscellaneous exercise?
faq.a: It mixes everything from the chapter — matrix polynomials such as A² − 5A + 6I, finding inverses from a matrix equation, expressing a matrix as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix, and solving matrix equations like AX = B.

faq.q: How do you write a square matrix as a symmetric plus a skew-symmetric matrix?
faq.a: Use A = ½(A + A′) + ½(A − A′). The first term is symmetric because (A + A′)′ = A + A′, and the second is skew-symmetric because (A − A′)′ = −(A − A′).

faq.q: How do you find the inverse of A from an equation like A² − 4A + 3I = O?
faq.a: Multiply the whole equation by A⁻¹. Every A term drops by one power, leaving an expression for A⁻¹ in terms of A and I — here A⁻¹ = ⅓(4I − A). No cofactor work is needed.

faq.q: Why does the order matter when solving matrix equations?
faq.a: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so AX = B and XA = B have different solutions. For AX = B you pre-multiply by A⁻¹ to get X = A⁻¹B; for XA = B you post-multiply to get X = BA⁻¹.
